title: Efficient equivariant framework for universal charge density prediction - Nature Machine Intelligence
text:
A preprint version of the article is available at arXiv.

AbstractAccelerating materials discovery requires efficient electronic structure calculations, which remain a critical challenge owing to the high computational cost of density functional theory. While charge density plays a central role in determining electronic structures in density functional theory, existing generalizable machine learning (ML) charge density models are hindered by prohibitive computational costs. Here we present the Equivariant Density Graph Neural Network (EdenGNN), an ML charge density model for electronic structure to overcome these limitations. It predicts both charge density and augmentation occupancies, enabling electronic structure calculations with projector augmented-wave accuracy. Critically, by using a basis-expansion formulation with fully trainable radial basis functions and a Δ-learning strategy to capture charge transfer, it is more than an order of magnitude faster. Notably, trained on the Materials Project database, our universal model for non-magnetic structures across the periodic table, EdenGNN-Uni, accurately predicts the band structures for most unseen materials across a vast chemical space, demonstrating enhanced robustness over universal ML Hamiltonian methods. These findings establish the ML charge density model as a scalable ab initio method for large-scale electronic structure calculations and high-throughput screening.

Data availability

The datasets, model parameters and pseudopotential versions used in this work are available via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21533014 (ref. 64). Source data are provided with this paper.
Code availability

The source code of EdenGNN is available via GitHub at https://github.com/rubenlee11/EdenGNN (ref. 65). The repository contains the source code, documentation and scripts necessary to reproduce the main experiments. Importantly, the spatial distribution of DFT charge density is sensitive to DFT calculations parameters such as the cutoff energy and accuracy settings. As ML models are inherently trained on specific pseudopotentials and DFT settings, applying the pretrained models for downstream tasks strictly requires consistent computational setups.
